messages:
Alex (Sales): Quick sync on ACME enterprise commit. They sent SOW asking for reserved capacity + autoscale hedge. Customer expects peak traffic of ~3,500 req/min (≈58 RPS) for chat endpoints during 9–5 PST, with tail bursts up to 2x that for launches. Also returned security questionnaire — legal is waiting on KMS + audit answers. Need: sizing, pricing delta for reserved vs burst, and a fallback runbook for AZ failures.

Mira (Solutions): Can you paste the traffic profile they shared? seq lengths, model family, and % streaming vs sync? Those change GPU mapping a lot.

Alex (Sales): From their doc: 95th percentile seq ~512 tokens, avg response 280 tokens. Model: open-llama-70b variant (quantized ok). 80% sync responses, 20% streaming. Peak window is 2 hours/day.

Jon (Infra): Quick rule of thumb: for that model + seq512 on A100-class GPUs (fp16) we estimate ~600–800 RPS per GPU for small single-turn requests. With 70B quantized (4-bit) that jumps to ~1,100–1,300 RPS. BUT sustained throughput and KV cache behavior matters for multi-turn chat. Given 58 RPS (3.5k/min) baseline, 1 reserved GPU is fine; for 2x burst we need headroom ~3 GPUs if we prefer capacity buffer.

Mira (Solutions): Suggest reserve 2 GPUs (to cover steady + some headroom) + an autoscale burst pool up to 4 GPUs. Autoscale policy: warm min=2, burst_max=4, scale_cooldown=60s. Use smaller quantized variant in burst as fallback to keep latency SLO.

Mira (Solutions): Example autoscale snippet:
```yaml
capacity_policy:
  reserved: 2
  burst_pool: 2
  scale_up_threshold: 0.75 # CPU/GPU util metric
  scale_down_threshold: 0.35
  cooldown: 60s
fallback_model: open-llama-70b-4bit
```

Sam (AE): Pricing angle: they asked for committed discount vs on-demand. We should quote reserved baseline + per-burst usage at spot/market rate with a cap. Can finance provide typical % discount bands for 6/12/24mo commits?

Jon (Infra): For SLAs we need to call out preheat/warmer strategy. If we rely on spot for burst, include a grace policy to fallback to smaller model and cross-AZ fallback. Also recommend prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts to cut token cost ~15–25%.

Tasha (Security): From the questionnaire: they require KMS with CMEK, full audit logs for inference requests (90 days), and VPC peering for Private deployment. These are gating for Private offering. Also want clarify data retention and deletion SLA (we have 30-day soft delete for prompt data by default). Legal will push if we don't confirm HSM/KMS details.

Alex (Sales): Noted. Action items: (1) Mira/Jon — produce sizing runbook for 2/3/4 GPU configs including latency percentiles and cost delta (compare fp16 reserved vs 4-bit burst); (2) Mira — draft autoscale YAML and fallback flows for their SREs; (3) Tasha — prepare brief answers for KMS/CMEK + retention to hand to legal. I'll give ACME a tentative quote with reserved 2 GPUs + burst up to 4.

Jon (Infra): I'll attach a quick perf sim this afternoon — will include p95 latency estimates at queued RPS and cold-start times per model variant. infra-bot: deploying perf sim job #acme-sizing-2281.

infra-bot: perf-sim job started: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf-sim/2281 (logs streaming).

Mira (Solutions): Also recommend we offer a small canary period with autoscale thresholds tuned (1 week) + a rollback plan: if p95 > 600ms for >5min, fallback to smaller model and notify oncall.

Sam (AE): I'll flag pricing bands with finance and loop legal for the questionnaire. Alex — can you confirm whether ACME will accept Private (VPC) or they want Hosted with contractual KMS? That changes ops overhead.

Alex (Sales): They prefer Hosted but want CMEK and audit logs — sounds like Private is cleaner. I'll confirm.

Tasha (Security): If they go Private we'll need to schedule a network call for peering and KMS key exchange. Also check whether they require FedRAMP/EU data residency.

Alex (Sales): Great. I'll update ACME and schedule a tech call tomorrow 10am PST. Thanks all — please drop the sizing artifacts and I'll consolidate for the quote. :thumbsup:
